- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often over-forecasts downward; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- Model consistently over-estimates short-term spikes (e.g., +3–5% above true peak) — cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent high.
- Model under-estimates mean reversion after strong rallies — add 0.3–0.8% downward bias in 3–5 day horizon if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag true trend by 1–3 days; apply 0.5–1.0% upward bias if sentiment remains bullish or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bounce” patterns (e.g., +0.33, +1.00, +0.33), model under-reacts — increase forecast by 0.2–0.5% for next 3–5 days.
